prompt:
Find real, peer-reviewed or preprint studies measuring how often large language models fabricate citations. Cite the papers and quote the fabrication rates they report.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

If you're not sure about something, just say so.

response.content:
Recent studies indicate that large language models (LLMs) frequently fabricate bibliographic citations, with rates varying significantly by model version, topic familiarity, and prompt specificity. Below are the findings from peer-reviewed and preprint studies quantifying these fabrication rates.

**GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 Performance**
A study published in *Scientific Reports* evaluated citation fabrication in GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 across 42 multidisciplinary topics. The researchers found a substantial reduction in hallucinations from GPT-3.5 to GPT-4, though significant error rates remained.

SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-41032-5 | QUOTE: "Within this set of documents, 55% of the GPT-3.5 citations but just 18% of the GPT-4 citations are fabricated." | CLAIM: GPT-3.5 fabricated 55% of citations, while GPT-4 fabricated 18%.

**GPT-4o Performance in Mental Health Research**
A 2025 experimental study published in *JMIR* examined GPT-4o (Omni) when generating literature reviews on mental health disorders. The study highlighted that fabrication rates depend on how well-known the topic is; less familiar disorders resulted in higher fabrication rates.

SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12658395/ | QUOTE: "Across the 6 reviews, GPT-4o generated 176 citations; 35 (19.9%) were fabricated." | CLAIM: GPT-4o fabricated 19.9% of citations overall in mental health literature reviews.

SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12658395/ | QUOTE: "Fabrication rates differed significantly by disorder... with higher rates for binge eating disorder (17/60, 28%) and body dysmorphic disorder (14/48, 29%) than for major depressive disorder (4/68, 6%)." | CLAIM: Fabrication rates for GPT-4o ranged from 6% for major depressive disorder to 29% for body dysmorphic disorder.

The study also noted that specialized prompts increased fabrication risks for certain topics.

SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12658395/ | QUOTE: "stratified analyses showed higher fabrication for specialized versus general reviews of binge eating disorder (11/24, 46% vs 6/36, 17%; P=.01)." | CLAIM: For binge eating disorder, specialized prompts led to a 46% fabrication rate compared to 17% for general prompts.

**Cross-Model Audit of 10 LLMs**
A large-scale audit presented in a 2026 arXiv preprint tested 10 commercially deployed LLMs across four academic domains. This study found a wide variance in performance depending on the specific model and domain.

SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03299 | QUOTE: "Our results show that the observed hallucination rates span a fivefold range (between 11.4% and 56.8%) and are strongly shaped by model, domain, and prompt framing." | CLAIM: Across 10 different LLMs, citation fabrication rates ranged from 11.4% to 56.8%.

**Prevalence in Published Literature**
While the above studies measure model output directly, another study investigated whether these fabricated citations make it into published scientific literature. Although the rate in published papers is low, the existence of such errors highlights integrity vulnerabilities.

SOURCE: https://www.mdpi.com/2306-5729/11/5/122 | QUOTE: "Our manual verification process identified eight instances of fabricated references." | CLAIM: In an analysis of 127,063 references from 3,541 published papers, only eight fabricated references were found, indicating a low but present prevalence in peer-reviewed literature.
